tool.title: Derive the metamodel an ArchiMate model uses, and check it against ArchiMate's relationship table
tool.description: For each model an instance's `cat-archimate.config.json` names: the element types it uses, with counts; every (source type, relationship, target type) pattern its relationships follow, with counts and ids; whether ArchiMate's relationship table (Appendix B of ArchiMate 3.2, as Archi holds it, committed as `archimate/schemas/archimate-relationships.json` in the tools layer) allows each pattern; and the placeholder elements, named after their own type, that a hand-drawn metamodel leaves in a model. Prints a report, JSON, Graphviz DOT or a Mermaid class diagram. `archimate-pages` draws the same result on each model's "Metamodel in use" page, so the metamodel is derived, never drawn.

inputs.name: instance
inputs.description: The instance root whose ArchiMate models are read.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: One model's id from the config; absent, every model. Required for `--format dot` and `mmd`.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Exit 1 when any relationship follows a pattern ArchiMate does not allow. Placeholders are reported, never fatal.

outputs.name: metamodel
outputs.description: The report, or the metamodel as `archimate-metamodel/v1` JSON, DOT or Mermaid, on stdout.

selection.when: Before publishing an ArchiMate model (process `archimate-publish`, after `archimate-check`), in its CI, and whenever someone asks which element types and relationships a model actually uses — instead of drawing a metamodel view by hand.
selection.limits: Checks each relationship's type against its ends' types only; it does not check derivation chains, viewpoints or properties. A type the table does not know is reported as not checked, never as refused.
selection.cost: One parse per model and a table lookup per relationship; milliseconds. No network, no JVM.
